correctness.rationale: Equations (8), (10), and (15) of arXiv:2311.15359 give exactly the specified floor-based rank sets and fixed population normalizers. The extended sine-power bump is C3, with first three derivatives zero at the joins; the derivative of the perturbed quantile is everywhere greater than 0.8015. The inverse thus has a positive C2 density, and tail equality plus change at the midpoint excludes the entire Lévy scale family. The claim for the displayed density is C2, not C-infinity; genuinely C-infinity compactly supported bumps also work under the monotonicity condition. Under common uniforms, both samples maintain ranks and agree on every used order statistic when N_p>=k and N_q<ell. The coupling inequality gives the TV bound, hence also controls every rejection probability based on this statistic. Stirling at the near-threshold masses and Chernoff upper bounds prove the two binomial exponents, with the lower excursion dominating. Conditional on N_p=k-1, the added count up to q is Bin(n-k+1,1/2), and lies between 1 and ell-k with probability tending to one. That event strictly raises the lower band while leaving the upper band unchanged, proving the matching exponent for this coupling only. The one-point CDF separation distinguishes the full samples. No sharp TV lower bound or ensemble-test conclusion is inferred.

value.rationale: The result exposes a concrete detection limit of an actually specified goodness-of-fit test, uniformly over all rejection rules based on its statistic, even though an elementary statistic on the full data separates the same alternatives.
